title: First home buyer entitlements for a Queensland purchase (QLD grant and duty concessions, federal First Home Guarantee)
disclaimer: DRAFT. General information only, not financial or legal advice. Results are indicative and must be confirmed with Queensland Revenue Office, Housing Australia and a participating lender. Program rules change; check the effective date and sources shown.

rules.title: Queensland First Home Owner Grant
rules.failureReason: Not eligible on the answers given. The grant is for new homes valued under $750,000, for first home owners who will live in the home.

benefit.description: One-off grant of $30,000 for contracts signed on or after 20 November 2023

sources.title: QRO: First home owner grant eligibility

assumptions: Contract is signed (or foundations laid, for owner-builders) on or after 20 November 2023.
No end date for the $30,000 amount was stated on the QRO page when retrieved; confirm before relying on it.
Substantially renovated homes can qualify in limited cases; not modelled here.

rules.title: First home concession for a new home (transfer duty)
rules.failureReason: Not eligible on the answers given. This concession is for first home buyers of a new home they will live in.

benefit.description: No transfer duty on the residential land for eligible transactions on or after 1 May 2025, with no cap on the home's value

sources.title: QRO: First home concession (new homes and vacant land)

assumptions: Standard duty still applies to any extra land that is not residential.
Full residence conditions are on the QRO eligibility tester and have not been encoded.

rules.title: First home vacant land concession (transfer duty)
rules.failureReason: Not eligible on the answers given. This concession is for first home buyers buying land to build a home they will live in.

benefit.description: No transfer duty on residential vacant land for eligible transactions on or after 1 May 2025, with no cap on the land's value

sources.title: QRO: First home concession (new homes and vacant land)

assumptions: Full conditions (such as building time frames) are on the QRO eligibility tester and have not been encoded.

rules.title: First home concession for an established home (transfer duty)
rules.failureReason: Not eligible on the answers given. This concession is for first home buyers of an established home under $800,000 they will live in.

benefit.description: Reduction in transfer duty (contracts signed on or after 9 June 2024)

assumptions: The $17,350 top band and $1,735 bottom band are from QRO; the intermediate bands assume equal $1,735 steps per $10,000 and must be checked against the QRO table.
This is a reduction to the home concession duty amount, not the total duty payable.

rules.title: Federal First Home Guarantee (5% deposit, no lenders mortgage insurance)
rules.failureReason: Not eligible on the answers given. The guarantee needs owner-occupiers with at least a 5% deposit, no property owned in the last 10 years, and a price within the local cap ($1,000,000 in Brisbane, Gold Coast and Sunshine Coast; $700,000 elsewhere in Queensland).

benefit.description: Government guarantee of up to 15% of the property value, so you can buy with a 5% deposit without lenders mortgage insurance. Places are unlimited from 1 October 2025.

sources.title: Housing Australia: Unlimited places, higher property price caps from 1 October 2025

assumptions: Income caps: the 1 October 2025 announcement removes them, but the First Home Guarantee page still listed $125,000 single / $200,000 joint when retrieved. This pack follows the announcement; confirm with Housing Australia.
Approval is by a participating lender, who may need a larger deposit.

openQuestions: Conflicting sources on Home Guarantee income caps (see AU-HGS-FHG assumptions).
QRO intermediate duty concession bands to be checked against the published table.
Shared-equity (Help to Buy) and QLD-specific schemes are not yet encoded.
Income band: no program in this pack currently depends on income, so the FHB questionnaire should not ask for it (V11 §12.5 minimisation). Revisit if a means-tested program is added.
